docs.title: Documentation
docs.about: The database collects {n} shear and compression tests on modern masonry walls reported in the literature. Data are primarily taken from Morandi et al. (2018) and Morandi & Albanesi (2026), and further complemented.
docs.filesIntro: Every file is identified by the specimen number N from the database table. Curves are stored as drift [%] and force [kN].

others.title: Other projects from the lab
others.lead: The Modern Masonry Database is one of the open datasets published by the Earthquake Engineering and Structural Dynamics laboratory.

submit.title: New submission
submit.lead: Add in-plane shear-compression tests to the Modern Masonry Database: fill or import the specimen metadata, attach the measured responses and photos. Everything is checked automatically as you go.
submit.p1: Start from the starter kit: it is the submission folder laid out the way it should be — the template CSV with the database's {n} column headers, and one example file per response type. Fill in one row per specimen (the data dictionary says what each column expects), then drop the whole folder here.
submit.p2a: Measured responses are separate files, one per specimen, named after the specimen they belong to
submit.p2c: and placed in the folder of their type. Drop the folder, a zip of it, or the files themselves: they are matched to the specimens by name.
submit.p3: Curves are stored as drift [%] and horizontal force [kN]; envelopes and bilinear idealisations come as one file per loading direction.
submit.dropTitle: Drop your submission folder here — or a zip, or CSV files
submit.dropText: The specimens CSV, plus one file per specimen and response type, named after the specimen, in its folder: 02_fd_curve, 03_envelope, 04_bilinear_curve, and photos in 05_fig_setup to 08_fig_cracks. Files are matched by name; what cannot be placed is listed below for you to sort out.
submit.warning: Add at least one specimen with a name and a reference to enable the automatic check.
submit.note: Submitting opens a review request on {repo} — a curator approves it before the data goes live.
submit.layoutIntro: What the submission folder looks like; drop it whole on the editor.

submit.readme:
Modern Masonry Database — submission starter kit

ModernMasonryDatabase_EIA_Database.csv: one row per specimen, {n} columns. Leave N blank: the curator assigns it. The row for SW0.1 is an example; replace it.

Response files are named after the specimen and placed in the folder of their type:
  02_fd_curve/fd_curve_{s}.csv
  03_envelope/envelope_{s}_pos.csv and _neg.csv
  04_bilinear_curve/bilinear_{s}_pos.csv and _neg.csv
  05_fig_setup/ … 08_fig_cracks/fig_{k}_{s}.jpg

Curves have two columns: drift [%], horizontal_force [kN].
The column definitions are in the data dictionary on the Documentation page.
